doc.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Musical family: father the cantor, brothers and sisters
summary: His father became a cantor, his mother sang a little, and he and brother Sam are the family's professionals.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well they certainly had musical children. Were they musical at all?

Yes, but not professionally. My father wound up being the cantor of a small synagogue, this was years and years later. He’d always wanted to do that sort of thing. And he called himself, I call him a cantor, but it was like a congregation of about maybe twenty people. Now he was the fellow who did the liturgical work so he was the cantor for the group. But that was his pride and joy I remember. He really used to like to do that. And my mother sang a little bit, just for the kids. The other kids were musical in a way. My

brother, we have three brothers and two sisters. Bernie, my youngest brother, likes to play guitar and sing a little bit. And Sam of course, that’s the middle brother, he’s a twin you know. But she, Ruth, his twin, wasn’t into music. The other sister, which is Fran, sings a bit, she likes to sing. And that takes care of the family. So Sam and I are the only professionals let’s call them. Bernie likes to do it.
